Background

His works often depicted scenes of nature, especially the changing seasons, and the artist's response to these natural phenomena. He used bold colour and loose brushwork to evoke the sensation of light and atmosphere.
Monet was born in Paris, but spent much of his life in Giverny, a village 45 kilometres (28 mi) from Paris. He studied art in Le Havre and at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris. He initially painted portraits and academic subjects, but soon began to paint en plein air, capturing the effects of light on the landscape. He was a founding member of the Impressionist Exhibition Society and took part in all eight Impressionist exhibitions. In 1878, he purchased a boat and painted along the French coast and in England. In 1883, he painted in Algeria. He also designed gardens at Giverny, including the water garden and the pink and blue gardens. Monet's paintings brought him great fame during his lifetime and he was considered the most successful of the Impressionists. After his death in 1896, his paintings continued to be exhibited and he remained a highly influential artist.
